title: Nuh said: do your worst. I rely on Allah.
subtitle: Calm courage under pressure
then: The Prophet ﷺ was told to recite Nuh's story to Quraysh as a lesson. Ibn Kathir explains Nuh's words: {idea}if my preaching offends you, I do not care, and I will not stop.{/idea} {trap}Plot with all your idols and give me no respite.{/trap} He feared them not, because they stood on nothing.
now: Your whole team mocks the way you refuse to fudge the numbers. The pressure in the room is heavy. {idea}Nuh stood alone against a nation, calm.{/idea} You can stand in one meeting.
old: If everyone pushes against me, I have to give in.
new: When I rely on Allah, their pressure has nothing to stand on.
try: Hold to one right thing today that others pressure you to drop. Say bismillah first.

title: I never asked you for payment. My reward is Allah's.
subtitle: Advice given with no strings attached
then: Nuh said: {idea}I have not asked you anything for my advice. My reward is from Allah, and I am commanded to be a Muslim.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says {reward}Islam is the religion of all the prophets, first to last{/reward}; their laws differ, their religion is one.
now: You help a friend move house, fix a relative's CV, give honest advice. Part of you waits for the favour back. {reward}Nuh asked nothing, for centuries.{/reward} The reward was already arranged.
old: When I help, I expect something in return.
new: My reward is with Allah, so I can give advice and help freely.
try: Help someone today and tell no one, expecting nothing back.

title: The ark saved the few, the flood took the deniers.
subtitle: How Nuh's story ended
then: They denied Nuh, and Allah {reward}delivered him and those on his religion in the ark{/reward}, making them successors on the earth. {trap}Those who belied the signs were drowned.{/trap} Ibn Kathir says the message to the Prophet ﷺ was: see how We saved the believers.
now: You are the only one in your friend group who does not drink, or the only one at work who prays. It feels like being on a tiny boat. {reward}Allah saved the small boat.{/reward}
old: If I am in the minority, I must be wrong.
new: Being one of the few with Allah is safer than being one of the many without Him.
try: Thank Allah today for one person who shares your boat, and tell them you appreciate them.

title: Rejecting from the start seals the heart.
subtitle: When early refusal becomes a lock
then: After Nuh, messengers came to their peoples with clear proofs. Ibn Kathir says {trap}they would not believe because they had rejected it from the beginning.{/trap} He calls it {trap}a serious warning{/trap} to the Makkans who rejected the last Messenger ﷺ.
now: You decided years ago that a certain relative is always wrong. Now even when they say something wise, you cannot hear it. {trap}An early no hardens into a lock.{/trap} Keep the door open.
old: Once I have decided, nothing needs revisiting.
new: Rejecting before listening can seal my own heart.
try: Revisit one opinion you formed long ago. Ask Allah to show you the truth about it.

title: Musa and Harun came with signs, and met arrogance.
subtitle: Too proud to follow the truth
then: After those messengers, Allah sent Musa and Harun to Firaun and his chiefs with proofs. Ibn Kathir says {trap}they were too arrogant to follow the truth and submit to it.{/trap} The story is told to the Makkans, who also had power and pride.
now: Your younger colleague points out your mistake, politely and correctly. The hardest part is not the fix. {trap}It is swallowing your pride.{/trap} Arrogance blocks truth faster than doubt does.
old: I reject it because I am not convinced.
new: Sometimes the real block is pride, not lack of proof.
try: Accept one correction today from someone you would normally dismiss, and thank them.

title: Truth arrived, and they called it obvious magic.
subtitle: Labelling what they knew was true
then: Ibn Kathir says they spoke {trap}as if giving an oath{/trap}, but knew they were lying. He cites the verse: {trap}they denied them wrongfully and arrogantly, though they themselves were convinced.{/trap}
now: You know your friend was right in the argument. Instead you say, "Whatever, you always twist things." {trap}A label is easier than admitting it.{/trap} The truth does not change because you renamed it.
old: If I give it a dismissive name, I do not have to deal with it.
new: Labelling the truth does not change it. It only keeps me from it.
try: Admit one thing today you knew was true but kept brushing off.

title: Is this magic? Magicians never succeed.
subtitle: Musa's question to those who called truth a trick
then: Musa criticised them: {idea}do you say this about the truth when it has come to you? Is this magic?{/idea} He gave the test himself: {trap}magicians will never succeed.{/trap} Illusion fades. Truth stays.
now: The get-rich-quick scheme, the miracle diet, the viral life hack. They dazzle for a month. {idea}Check what is still standing a year later.{/idea} Truth has staying power. Tricks do not.
old: If it impresses me, it is probably real.
new: The real test is what lasts. Tricks never succeed in the end.
try: Think of one flashy promise you are tempted by. Ask: will this still stand in a year?

title: You want to pull us from our fathers' ways.
subtitle: Tradition and fear of losing power

row.title: what is true
sub: even if it is new to us

then: Firaun's chiefs said: {trap}have you come to turn us from what we found our fathers following, so you two can have greatness in the land?{/trap} Ibn Kathir explains greatness here as {trap}grandeur and leadership.{/trap} They feared losing both tradition and status.
now: "We have always done the wedding this way." "In our family we do not talk about that." Some traditions are beautiful. {trap}Some are just habits protecting someone's position.{/trap} Ask which one you are defending.
old: If my family always did it, it must be right.
new: I keep the good of my heritage, but truth outranks habit.
try: Pick one family habit and ask honestly: is this from Allah, or just from us?

title: Firaun summoned every skilled magician to beat the truth.
subtitle: Assembling experts against a clear sign
then: Ibn Kathir says Firaun {trap}wanted to deceive the people with the magicians' tricks{/trap} against the plain truth Musa brought. {reward}The result was the exact opposite.{/reward} In that public festival, the signs of the Lord prevailed.
now: You line up arguments, articles, and clever friends to win a point you know is weak. {trap}Expert help does not turn falsehood into truth.{/trap} Sometimes it backfires completely.
old: With enough experts on my side, I can win any argument.
new: No gathering of experts can defeat a clear truth from Allah.
try: Drop one argument today you are only defending to win.

title: Musa let them go first. Throw what you will.
subtitle: Letting falsehood show itself before the truth
then: The magicians lined up, promised closeness to Firaun and a big reward. Ibn Kathir says {idea}Musa wanted them to begin, so people would see what they made, and then the truth would triumph over it.{/idea} When their spells dazzled the crowd, {trap}Musa felt fear{/trap}, and Allah told him: fear not.
now: In a heated family discussion, you let the other person say everything first, without interrupting. {idea}Calm is a kind of confidence.{/idea} Truth does not need to shout first.
old: I must jump in first, or I will lose.
new: When I am on the side of truth, I can let others speak first.
try: In your next disagreement today, let the other person finish completely before you reply.

title: It is only magic, and Allah will undo it.
subtitle: Allah does not make corrupt work succeed
then: After the magicians cast, Musa said: {trap}what you have brought is sorcery.{/trap} {idea}Allah will make it of no effect. Allah does not set right the work of evildoers.{/idea} His staff swallowed what they made.
now: A shortcut at work: a padded invoice, a hidden flaw in the report. It seems to hold. {idea}Allah does not bless corrupt work.{/idea} Sooner or later it unravels.
old: If no one catches it, the shortcut worked.
new: Allah does not set right corrupt work, so it never truly works.
try: Fix one small dishonest shortcut in your work or habits today.

title: Allah makes the truth stand, whoever hates it.
subtitle: Truth established by His words
then: Musa finished: {idea}Allah will establish the truth by His words, however much the criminals hate it.{/idea} Ibn Kathir notes that the magicians then {reward}fell down in prostration, saying we believe in the Lord of all that exists.{/reward}
now: You told the truth at work and someone powerful did not like it. The room went cold. {idea}Truth does not need everyone to like it.{/idea} Allah is the One who makes it stand.
old: If the powerful dislike the truth, it will be buried.
new: Allah establishes the truth, however much anyone hates it.
try: Say one true thing today kindly, even if you expect it will not be liked.

title: Only a few young people believed, despite the fear.
subtitle: Faith under a tyrant's shadow
then: Despite all the signs, {reward}only a few offspring of Firaun's people believed{/reward}, among them Firaun's wife and the believer who hid his faith. They feared {trap}Firaun would force them back.{/trap} Ibn Kathir says Firaun was {trap}an evil tyrant and extremely arrogant.{/trap}
now: You are the first in your family to start praying regularly. You are nervous about the jokes at dinner. {reward}Faith does not wait for fear to leave.{/reward} The young believers had more to lose, and still believed.
old: I will take faith seriously once it is easy and safe.
new: Faith can begin even while I am afraid.
try: Do one act of faith today that you have been too shy to do in front of others.

title: If you believe in Allah, then rely on Him.
subtitle: Faith shows itself in trust
then: Musa told the Children of Israel, under Firaun's pressure, to {reward}put their trust in Allah.{/reward} Ibn Kathir says {idea}Allah is sufficient for those who trust Him{/idea}, and notes how often worship and reliance appear together, as in {idea}You alone we worship, You alone we ask for help.{/idea}
now: The redundancy email. The test results pending. You pray, and then lie awake running every bad scenario. {reward}Faith includes letting Him carry it.{/reward} You say it in every prayer: You alone we ask for help.
old: I believe in Allah, but I still have to carry everything myself.
new: Believing in Allah means trusting Him with what I cannot carry.
try: In your next prayer, say iyyaka nasta'in slowly, and hand Him one specific worry.
